method: Feature-by-feature content reconciliation of the normative G1 spec/registry against the canonical Rust core, documented historical Python reference, and source-level tests at an exact source head. Source presence is not test execution.

limitations: Content-level source review only; no CI or test execution performed for this matrix.
Feature classification is about evidenced coverage at the exact source head, not a claim that every unlisted construct is absent from every subsystem.
The Python reference is represented by checked-in documentation and historical expected JSON, not a live executable differential oracle.

summary.headline: The canonical Rust parser is a deliberate, fail-closed subset; G1 spec/registry and provenance still describe a broader Python-reference language. Equivalence is not established.

features.finding: Rust lexer discards spaces/tabs/newlines as trivia; parser requires brace-delimited blocks. No indentation tokenization.
features.tests: Parser tests use brace-delimited source; no indentation positive/negative vectors located in the reviewed files.
features.action: Either implement indentation syntax in canonical Rust lexer/parser with golden tests, or approve a versioned syntax change and update spec+registry.

features.finding: Rust lexer recognizes '//' comments; '#' is not documented as a comment token in the Rust token enum/lexer.
features.tests: No cross-reference test for '#' versus '//' found in the reviewed test file.
features.action: Add positive/negative lexical vectors for both forms and resolve against normative language spec.

features.spec_claim: 63 token kinds including float/bytes/octal/binary, compound operators, logical/bitwise and layout tokens
features.finding: Rust Token enum exposes a much smaller token set: Int, Ident, Let/Const/Return/Fn/If/Else/While and a few operators/punctuation/string; no Float/Bytes/Indent/Dedent/compound operator inventory.
features.tests: Unit tests exercise a subset of arithmetic/comparison and malformed inputs; no evidence of full 63-token coverage.
features.action: Generate token-by-token positive and negative vectors from registry.json and reconcile each token with implementation.

features.spec_claim: Decimal, hex, octal, binary, float, string, bytes, booleans and null
features.finding: Rust core AST/lexer explicitly model Int and String, but no Float, bytes, boolean or null literal variants in the reviewed source.
features.tests: Current parser primary expression accepts integer, identifier and parenthesized expression; no vectors proving other literal classes.
features.action: Add registry-derived literal vectors or explicitly exclude unsupported literal classes in a versioned language profile.

features.finding: Some reserved tokens appear in the lexer and a separate native contract parser exists, but the core parser top-level accepts only let/const/fn. Full keyword-to-production coverage is not established.
features.tests: native.rs contains contract semantic tests; no registry-wide keyword coverage was identified.
features.action: Map each keyword to core grammar, native DSL, delegated API, or unsupported status; add negative tests for accidental acceptance.

features.spec_claim: 84 type identifiers including generics, collection, blockchain, OS and aliases
features.finding: Core parser reads a type annotation as a single identifier; AST TypeHint stores one name and serializes params as empty. This does not establish generic/nested type grammar or semantic support for the registry's 84 names.
features.tests: Typed function parameters are tested; no registry-wide type matrix located.
features.action: Create a type-name and type-expression matrix, separating lexically accepted names from semantically supported types.

features.spec_claim: module declaration plus broad statement grammar
features.finding: program() accepts only let, const and fn at top level and errors on other token kinds; module declarations and contract/struct/enum/class productions are not handled by this core parser.
features.tests: Negative test explicitly asserts top-level return is rejected; no module declaration conformance test in parser.rs.
features.action: Decide whether the core is a named profile/subset; otherwise implement missing productions and tests.

features.spec_claim: if/elif/else, for, while, loop, break, continue, match/case, emit, require, return
features.finding: Core AST has Let/Fn/Return/Expr/If/While. Parser supports if/else/else-if via nesting and while; other listed statement forms are not represented in the core AST.
features.tests: Parser tests cover if/else/else-if/while. End-to-end tests cover return and fail-closed lowering; no evidence for for/match/emit/require in core parser.
features.action: For each registry production assign implemented/delegated/unsupported/unresolved and add parse + lowering + runtime tests as applicable.

features.spec_claim: Logical, bitwise, shifts, exponentiation, ranges, assignments, casts, postfix/member/index/lambda and full precedence table
features.finding: Core expression grammar covers comparison, addition, multiplication, unary, call postfix and primary; AST covers int/identifier/unary/binary/call. Member/index/range/lambda/cast and many operators are not represented.
features.tests: Precedence/associativity and comparison precedence tests exist; end-to-end test expects '%' to fail closed.
features.action: Generate operator and expression-node coverage from the normative registry; test precedence and explicit rejection of unsupported operators.

features.finding: Rust AST defines a small node family (Expr Int/Ident/Unary/Binary/Call; Stmt Let/Fn/Return/Expr/If/While), far fewer than the registry's documented AST node inventory.
features.tests: Differential harness compares canonical JSON for a shared subset only.
features.action: Version the AST profile and add per-node mappings; do not claim full AST conformance from subset differential tests.

features.spec_claim: Semantics registry, type checker, scope and capability rules
features.finding: Reviewed Rust core performs fail-closed lowering checks and value/runtime checks; the full historical Python semantic pipeline is documented, not present as a runnable Python implementation in the current tree. Complete SEM-rule mapping is not established.
features.tests: End-to-end tests cover unknown identifiers/functions, arity mismatch, overflow, division by zero and call-depth failure. They do not prove all normative semantic rules.
features.action: Map every SEM rule to Rust symbol, negative/positive tests and explicit owner; classify rules not in the current profile.

features.spec_claim: SPEC/registry claim Python reference at src/atclang, commit a7e1bd4
features.finding: Current architecture and README describe Rust as canonical and Python as legacy/unverified documentation; README says Python reference has been removed from the repository and documented under docs/reference/python. The normative spec/registry still name the old Python source as the source of truth.
features.tests: Differential test consumes checked-in corpus and expected JSON; it does not execute Python reference at test time.
features.action: Correct normative source-of-truth metadata through versioned governance, or restore reproducible archived reference evidence; do not mark G1 passed based on stale provenance.

features.spec_claim: Rust and Python canonical AST output match
features.finding: A test harness compares Rust JSON against checked-in expected JSON for the shared subset; source comments say expected files were generated from Python. This is not live reference differential execution and its runtime result was not checked in this task.
features.tests: Test function differential_gemeinsamer_subset; no run/job/step/exit-code evidence collected here.
features.action: Run exact-head CI, capture Run→Job→Step/exit code and artifact hashes; document corpus count and exclusions.

features.finding: Separate native contract parser and semantic validator exist, but its grammar's relationship to normative G1 grammar and normal parse/lower/execute pipeline is not fully mapped.
features.tests: native.rs contains validate_contract_semantics test surface; no cross-path conformance map observed.
features.action: Define whether native DSL is a separate profile or part of core grammar; add end-to-end fixtures and exact mapping.

features.spec_claim: Canonical AST serialization compatible with reference
features.finding: Rust manually serializes its subset AST into JSON with fixed key order; differential harness compares to checked-in expected files. This proves intended subset design, not full registry AST compatibility.
features.tests: Parser tests assert selected JSON fragments; differential harness exists but no run evidence in this matrix task.
features.action: Add schema/golden tests for all supported node variants and ensure canonical JSON escaping and ordering are exhaustive.

features.spec_claim: Normative full language with fail-closed behavior
features.finding: Lowering documents fail-closed behavior for unsupported forms; this is a sound safety boundary but does not make the supported subset equivalent to the full language spec.
features.tests: run.rs explicitly checks unsupported '%' and unknown names/functions fail.
features.action: Publish a normative Rust subset profile and keep unsupported constructs explicitly rejected until implemented.

required_decisions: Define and version the intended production language profile: full G1 grammar versus explicitly named Rust core subset.
Resolve indentation blocks versus brace blocks and '#' versus '//' comments against the normative spec.
Map every registry token, keyword, type, namespace, parser production, AST node and semantic rule to an implementation symbol and positive/negative test or documented exclusion.
Fix stale G1 source-of-truth metadata: current repo documents Rust canonical and Python historical/unverified, while the spec/registry cite Python source as authority.
Run exact-head CI and preserve Run→Job→Step→exit-code/log evidence; only then assign VERIFIED to individual contracts.
